login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Welcome back. Sign in to manage your devices.
login.totpSubtitle: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.
login.useLocal: Sign in with a local account

password.mismatch: The new passwords do not match.
password.rules: At least 12 characters, not containing your username. A sentence of a few words works well.

totp.step1: Open an authenticator app such as Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or 1Password.
totp.step2: Scan the QR code, or enter the key by hand, and type the code it shows.
totp.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app

firstLogin.title: Choose a new password
firstLogin.subtitle: You signed in as {{user}} with a one-time password. Choose your own password to continue.
firstLogin.totpSubtitle: Your password is changed. We recommend two-factor authentication with an authenticator app, especially for the administrator account.

profile.title: Profile
profile.subtitle: Your account, language and security.
profile.twoFactorHint: A code from an authenticator app is asked after your password.
profile.totpDisableHint: Enter your password to turn off two-factor authentication.
profile.managedByEntra: You sign in with Microsoft Entra ID; multi-factor authentication is handled there.
profile.passwordSaved: Your password is changed. Other sessions were signed out.

users.title: Users & roles
users.subtitle: Local accounts and accounts that signed in with Entra ID. Roles decide what each person may do.
users.name: Name
users.roleFromEntra: Set by the role mappings at every Microsoft sign-in.
users.breakGlassRole: The emergency account is always an administrator.
users.initialPasswordHint: Leave empty to generate a one-time password. The user must choose a new password at the first sign-in.
users.disableHint: A disabled user cannot sign in; open sessions end right away.
users.resetHint: {{user}} gets a new one-time password and is signed out everywhere.
users.oneTimeHint: Give this password to {{user}} in a safe way. It is shown only once and must be changed at the first sign-in.
users.rolesSubtitle: Built-in roles and what they allow. Technicians and read-only users can be limited to device groups.
users.scopeFromEntra: The device groups come from the role mappings at every Microsoft sign-in.

roles.administratorDesc: Everything, including users, settings and updates.
roles.technicianDesc: Manage devices: patches, software, remote control.
roles.readonlyDesc: View the dashboard, devices and reports.

permissions.reports_manage: Manage report schedules and compliance rules
permissions.alerts_manage: Acknowledge alerts and manage alert rules
permissions.drivers_manage: Add drivers and firmware to the repository
permissions.remote_manage: Manage devices without taking over (processes, services, logs, files)

auth.title: Authentication
auth.subtitle: Local accounts always work. Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on is optional and off by default.
auth.entraSubtitle: Let people sign in with their Microsoft work account.
auth.enableHint: The local emergency administrator keeps working.
auth.tenantIdHint: Entra admin center > Overview > Tenant ID
auth.clientIdHint: From the overview page of your app registration.
auth.clientSecretHint: The secret value (not the secret ID) from Certificates & secrets.
auth.redirectUriHint: Add this as a Web redirect URI in the app registration. Set the public URL under Settings if it is wrong.
auth.testOk: Connection works: the tenant was found and the client secret is accepted.
auth.breakGlassSubtitle: The local "admin" account always stays available as a break-glass account. You can limit where it may sign in from.
auth.networksHint: Comma-separated IP addresses or CIDR ranges. Empty means everywhere. Your address now: {{ip}}
auth.mappingsSubtitle: Map Entra groups or app roles to FleetWarden roles. Roles are checked again at every sign-in.
auth.noMappings: No mappings yet. Without a mapping nobody can sign in with Microsoft.
auth.mappingsNote: When someone matches several mappings, the most privileged role wins. Users in more than 200 groups: use app roles.

mail.title: Mail server
mail.subtitle: Your own SMTP server for notifications, reports and alerts.
mail.enableHint: Queued messages are sent once mail is on.
mail.noneWarning: Without encryption, messages travel in clear text. Only use this for a relay on the local network. Password authentication is then not allowed.
mail.oauthHint: Uses the client credentials flow. The app registration needs the Exchange Online permission SMTP.SendAsApp and access to the mailbox in the username field.
mail.heloHint: Optional; the server host name by default.
mail.logSubtitle: The last 200 messages. Failed messages are retried up to 6 times.
mail.subject: Subject

branding.title: Branding
branding.subtitle: Your own name, logo and colours for the interface, the sign-in page and e-mails.
branding.productNameHint: Shown in the menu, the browser tab and e-mails. Empty: FleetWarden.
branding.logoHint: Square works best. SVG or PNG, up to 512 KB.
branding.faviconHint: Optional. Without one, the logo is used.

updates.title: Updates
updates.subtitle: Choose the update channel and update the server from here. A backup is made before every update, and a failed update is rolled back.
updates.channelHint: Production follows main; Test follows the test branch with the newest features.
updates.none: No release on this channel yet
updates.switchToProductionHint: You run a test build. Production updates are offered once production has a newer version than yours.
updates.confirm: Update to {{version}}? The server makes a backup, installs the update and restarts. The interface is unavailable for about a minute.

states.pending: Waiting for the updater to start…
states.rolled-back: Update failed and was rolled back

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: General server settings, agent scans and updates.
settings.scansSubtitle: How often agents send their software inventory and scan for missing Windows and Linux updates. Device groups can override these defaults.
settings.inventoryHint: Hardware, installed software and logged-on user. 15 minutes to 7 days.
settings.patchScanHint: Windows Update or apt. Only for devices in a group with a patch policy. 1 hour to 7 days.
settings.scansApplied: Online agents use the new interval within a minute.
settings.proxyHint: The public URL, trusted proxies, configuration examples and a connection test are on the Reverse proxy page.
settings.publicUrlHint: The address people use through your reverse proxy, used for SSO and links in e-mails. Empty: detected as {{url}}.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: Who did what and when: sign-ins, changes to users and settings, and updates.
audit.search: Search user, action, target or IP

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.subtitle: Encrypted full and incremental backups of the database and server files to one or more locations, with restore from the interface.
backup.runHere: Back up to this location now

setup.passBody: Every backup is encrypted with your passphrase before it leaves the server. Without it, backups cannot be made or restored.
setup.locBody: Choose where backups go: an SFTP/SCP or FTPS server, OneDrive, or a folder on this server such as a mounted network share.

stat.retention: Keeps {{count}} full backups with their incrementals

backup.locationsHint: Every backup goes to all enabled locations. Use at least one location outside this server.
backup.deleteLocationBody: Delete the location {{name}}? Backups already stored there are not removed and can still be restored with "Another location".
backup.noLocationsHint: Add an SFTP/SCP, FTPS or FTP server, a OneDrive, or a local folder.

typeHints.sftp: Any server with SSH access: a NAS (Synology, QNAP), a Linux server or a hosting account. Works wherever scp works.
typeHints.ftps: FTP with TLS encryption, for example FileZilla Server or a NAS. Self-signed certificates can be trusted after a test.
typeHints.ftp: Plain FTP. The backup itself is encrypted, but the password travels unencrypted.
typeHints.onedrive: Stores backups in the OneDrive of a Microsoft 365 user through an Entra app registration.
typeHints.local: A folder under /var/lib/fleetwarden/backups on this server, for example a mounted NAS share. Not a replacement for an off-site copy.

loc.name: Name
loc.implicitTlsHint: Only for servers that expect TLS right away (usually port 990). Most servers use explicit TLS on port 21.
loc.keyHint: Generate a key pair and add the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the backup user on the server, or paste your own private key.
loc.publicKeyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the backup server.
loc.onedriveHint: Uses an app registration in Microsoft Entra with the application permission Files.ReadWrite.All (admin consent). You can use the same app as for sign-in. See docs/backup.md for the steps.
loc.driveUserHint: User principal name of the account whose OneDrive stores the backups.
loc.pathHint: Folder on the server, relative to the home or root folder. Created when it does not exist.
loc.enabledHint: Disabled locations are skipped but can still be used for a restore.
loc.ftpWarning: FTP sends the password unencrypted. Use FTPS or SFTP when the server supports it.

trust.sshBody: The server presents this SSH host key. Compare it with the fingerprint on the server before you trust it.
trust.tlsBody: The server presents a certificate that is not issued by a trusted authority (for example self-signed). Check the SHA-256 fingerprint before you trust it.

repo.none: No backups at this location yet; the first backup creates the repository.
repo.wrong_passphrase: This location already holds FleetWarden backups made with another passphrase. Use another folder.
repo.unknown: Writing and deleting a test file works.

pass.title: Encryption passphrase
pass.subtitle: Backups are encrypted (AES-256) on this server with a key derived from this passphrase.
pass.warn: Store it in your password manager. To restore on a new server you need the passphrase; without it nobody, including you, can read the backups.
pass.label: Passphrase
pass.hint: At least 12 characters. A sentence works well.
pass.changeHint: Existing backups at reachable locations are re-keyed, so they can be restored with the new passphrase.

sched.title: Schedule and retention
sched.subtitle: Automatic backups: incremental ones in between, regularly a new full backup.
sched.enableHint: Missed backups (server off) run once when the server is back.
sched.fullEveryHint: The backups in between are incremental.
sched.keepHint: Older ones are deleted with their incrementals.
sched.summary: A full backup every {{full}} days, {{keep}} kept: you can go back about {{days}} days.

restore.title: Restore
restore.subtitle: Put the database and server files back from a backup. Also works on a new server: install FleetWarden, sign in and pick "Another location".
restore.otherHint: Enter the location and passphrase of the original server.
restore.passHint: The passphrase the backups were made with.
restore.snapshotsHint: Newest first. A full backup and its incrementals form a chain; each one can be restored on its own.
restore.newer: This backup was made with FleetWarden {{version}}, newer than this server. Update this server first.
restore.confirmBody: All current data (users, settings, history) is replaced by the backup. Everyone is signed out and the server restarts. A copy of the current state is kept on the server for a rollback.
restore.applyingBody: The server is restoring the backup and restarts. You will be taken to the sign-in page.
restore.stuck: Nothing happening? On a server without systemd, run the restore by hand:
restore.prepareFailed: The backup could not be prepared

backup.historyHint: The last 200 backups. A restore starts a new history.

scope.limitedHint: Only devices in the selected groups are visible and manageable.
scope.noneSelected: No group selected: this user sees no devices.

devices.title: Devices
devices.subtitle: Every enrolled workstation, server and Proxmox node, with live status and inventory.
devices.searchPlaceholder: Search name, user, IP, serial or OS
devices.emptyHint: Use Add client to get an installer and a ready-made command for Windows or Debian/Proxmox.
devices.selectAll: Select all devices on this page
devices.inventoryRequested: The agent is collecting a new inventory.
devices.deleteConfirm: Delete {{host}} and its inventory? A connected agent stops and forgets its enrollment; to manage the machine again, enroll it again.
devices.findOthers: Show every device with this program
devices.notesHint: Free text for your team, for example location or owner.
devices.noPackages: There are no packages for this platform in the library yet. Add one under

addClient.title: Add client

platformHints.windows: Windows 10/11 and Windows Server 2016 or newer
platformHints.linux: Debian 12/13, Ubuntu and Proxmox VE (amd64, arm64)

addClient.groupHint: New devices join this group. Each group gets its own token.
addClient.tokenUnusable: This token is revoked, expired or used up. Create a new one.
addClient.windowsCommand: Windows: run in an elevated PowerShell
addClient.windowsCommandHint: Downloads the MSI from this server, installs it silently and enrolls the device.
addClient.msiexec: Unattended install with msiexec (GPO, Intune, RMM)
addClient.linuxCommandHint: Downloads the .deb from this server, installs it and enrolls the device.
addClient.noPackage: This server has no agent package for this platform yet. Agent packages arrive with the server package or from Agent updates.
addClient.downloadHint: The server address and token are built into the download, so a double-click is enough.
addClient.manualHint: The installer wizard asks for these values:
addClient.waiting: Waiting for the device to enroll…
addClient.viaHint: Devices outside your network use a secure gateway. The commands and downloads below point at the address you pick.
addClient.viaDirect: Directly to this server (inside the network)

tokens.descriptionHint: Helps you recognise the token later, for example "Intune rollout".
tokens.title: Enrollment tokens
tokens.subtitle: Tokens let agents enroll into a group. Revoke a token when a script or installer leaked; enrolled devices keep working.
tokens.empty: No tokens yet. Add client creates one.
tokens.revokeConfirm: New devices can no longer enroll with this token. Devices that already enrolled are not affected.

groups.title: Groups
groups.subtitle: Device groups decide policies, update rings and which devices a role may manage.
groups.name: Name
groups.notEmpty: Move the devices out of this group first.
groups.ringHint: New agent versions reach ring 0 first, then the next rings.
groups.channelHint: For example a test group of pcs on the Test channel.
groups.windowLimit: Only update agents in a time window
groups.windowHint: Server time. A window like 22:00–06:00 runs past midnight.
groups.patchPolicyHint: When and how updates are installed on the devices in this group.

consentHint.auto: Servers and Proxmox nodes are taken over directly; on workstations the logged-on user is asked first.
consentHint.ask: The logged-on user must allow each session within 30 seconds. Without a logged-on user the session starts directly.
consentHint.notify: The session starts directly; the user sees a bar that someone is connected, with a button to end it.
consentHint.direct: The session starts without a notice, for servers and unattended computers.

agentUpdates.title: Agent updates
agentUpdates.subtitle: New agent versions come from GitHub or an upload and reach the device groups ring by ring.
agentUpdates.checked: Checked GitHub for new agent releases.
agentUpdates.rolloutsHint: A rollout starts with ring 0 (pilot). The next ring follows after the soak time; too many failed devices pause it.
agentUpdates.noOpenRollout: No rollout is running. Every agent runs the version its group should have.
agentUpdates.soakSummary: {{hours}} h per ring, pause after {{failures}} failures
agentUpdates.problemsHint: The agent reinstalled its previous version where it could. Use Retry on the rollout after fixing the cause.
agentUpdates.releasesHint: Groups without their own agent channel follow the server channel ({{channel}}). Production groups only receive releases.
agentUpdates.noReleases: No agent packages yet. Check GitHub or upload a package.
agentUpdates.startHint: Devices with an older agent receive this version, ring 0 first. A running rollout on the same channel is replaced.
agentUpdates.deleteConfirm: Delete the packages of version {{version}} from the server? Agents on this version can then no longer roll back to it.
agentUpdates.autoDownloadHint: Checks every hour for the channels your groups use.
agentUpdates.autoRollout: Start a rollout for each new release
agentUpdates.autoRolloutHint: Off: new versions are only downloaded, and you start rollouts yourself.
agentUpdates.soakHint: How long each ring runs before the next ring.
agentUpdates.maxFailuresHint: Failed devices per ring before the rollout pauses.
agentUpdates.keepReleasesHint: Older downloads are removed unless devices still run them.

patches.title: Patch management
patches.subtitle: Missing updates, approvals and maintenance windows for Windows, Debian and Proxmox.
patches.noPolicyText: Devices are only patched when their group has a patch policy.
patches.scanErrors_one: {{count}} device could not scan for updates. Open the device for the error.
patches.scanErrors_other: {{count}} devices could not scan for updates. Open the device for the error.

categoryHints.security: Security fixes, also security packages on Debian and Proxmox.
categoryHints.cumulative: Monthly cumulative updates and update rollups.
categoryHints.driver: Drivers now come through Drivers & firmware.
categoryHints.other: Other updates, and regular apt updates on Linux.

patches.missingUpdatesHint: Across all devices you may see. Approve or decline an update for every device at once.
patches.policiesHint: Assign a policy to device groups under Groups.

rebootHints.never: The device reports that it needs a restart; you restart it yourself.
rebootHints.automatic: Restarts right after installing. A logged-on user sees a countdown first.
rebootHints.prompt: The user may postpone the restart; after the last postpone it restarts anyway.

patches.deletePolicyConfirm_one: Delete {{name}}? {{count}} group will no longer be patched.
patches.deletePolicyConfirm_other: Delete {{name}}? {{count}} groups will no longer be patched.
patches.enabledHint: When off, devices still scan on request but nothing is installed automatically.
patches.windowHint: Jobs only start inside the window; a window may run past midnight. Devices that are offline get their updates in the next window.
patches.approvalsHint: Automatic approval can wait a number of days after release, so problems with an update show up first. A manual approval or decline under Updates always wins.
patches.notifyUsersHint: Before installing, Windows shows a pop-up at the bottom right. Restarts always show one. Without a logged-on user the job goes ahead right away.
patches.countdownHint: Without an answer the job goes ahead.
patches.takeOverHint: Turns off Windows' own automatic installs, so updates only arrive in the window. Devices that get updates from Intune or a WSUS GPO: choose one tool to be in charge.
patches.deviceNoPolicy: This device's group has no patch policy. Set one under
patches.scanRequested: The device is scanning for updates.
patches.installStarted: The patch job was sent to the device.
patches.upToDate: Up to date: no missing updates.
patches.scanIntervalMoved: How often devices scan for updates is set under Settings > Agent scans, and per device group.
patches.driversSectionHint: Only updates that an administrator added to the driver repository are installed, in this window and with the restart settings below. Devices never download drivers from the vendor themselves.
patches.driversHint: Also stops Windows from fetching drivers by itself when a device is plugged in.
patches.firmwareHint: Firmware needs a restart. On Windows BitLocker is suspended for that one restart. Test on a few devices first.

software.title: Software
software.subtitle: Your software library, and everything installed across your devices.
software.libraryHint: Packages you can roll out to devices and groups.
software.emptyText: Add software from the winget catalog, upload your own MSI or EXE installer, or add an apt package for Linux.
software.deleteText: Delete {{name}} from the library? Software that is already installed stays on the devices, and past deployments keep their history.

catalog.title: Winget catalog
catalog.hint: The server downloads the public winget catalog once a day. Devices download installers straight from the vendor and check the SHA-256 hash from the catalog.

software.installedHint: From the inventory of every device you can see. Uninstall removes the program from every device that has it, or the devices you pick.

kinds.exeHint: Enter the silent install arguments from the vendor.
kinds.debHint: Installed with apt-get, which also fetches the dependencies.

deploy.platformHint: Only devices with this platform are shown.
deploy.ongoing: Keep the groups up to date
deploy.ongoingHint: Devices that join these groups later get the job too.
deploy.uninstallArgsHint: Optional. FleetWarden uses the quiet uninstaller when the program has one, and msiexec /x for MSI packages. Add the vendor's silent arguments here when it doesn't.
deploy.purgeHint: Uses apt-get purge instead of remove.
deploy.laterHint: Pick when the devices may start.
deploy.expireHint: Devices that haven't started by then are marked as expired.
deploy.browsersHint: Devices update to the newest version from the winget catalog, in their own language and edition (Firefox ESR stays ESR). If a browser is open, the user gets a pop-up with a 60-second countdown and can postpone it as often as their patch policy allows. The browser then closes, updates and opens again with its windows and tabs.

source.wingetHint: Search thousands of applications. Always the official installer from the vendor.
source.uploadHint: Your own MSI or EXE for Windows, or a .deb for Linux.
source.aptHint: A package from the repositories your Linux devices already use.

form.aptPackageHint: The exact package name, such as htop or curl.
form.noInstaller: This package has no installer FleetWarden can run silently for all users.
form.versionHint: Latest always installs the newest version from the catalog.
form.catalogEmpty: The winget catalog hasn't been loaded yet. Close this window and refresh the catalog first.
form.searchCatalog: Search the winget catalog, such as Chrome or 7-Zip
form.dropFile: Drop an installer here (.msi, .exe or .deb, up to {{size}} GB)
form.argsWinget: Optional. Added to the silent arguments from the catalog.
form.argsMsi: Optional MSI properties, such as ALLUSERS=1 or a license key.
form.argsRequired: Required. Find the silent arguments in the vendor's documentation, such as /S or /quiet.
form.name: Name
form.fileVersionHint: Optional. Devices with this version or newer are skipped.
form.detectNameHint: Used to see if the program is already installed. Defaults to the package name.
form.productCodeHint: Optional. The most precise way to detect an MSI.
form.anyHashHint: Some vendors replace the installer behind the same link (such as Chrome). Turn this on only for vendors you trust.

browsers.noCatalog: The winget catalog hasn't been loaded yet. Refresh it under Library to see the newest versions and update browsers.
browsers.allUpToDate: All browsers are up to date.
browsers.onlyOutdated: Only devices with an outdated browser

deployments.title: Deployments
deployments.subtitle: Software installs and uninstalls, with the result of every device.
deployments.emptyText: Pick a package in the software library and choose Deploy.
deployments.cancelled: The deployment is cancelled. Jobs that are running finish first.
deployments.rebootNeeded_one: {{count}} device needs a restart to finish.
deployments.rebootNeeded_other: {{count}} devices need a restart to finish.
deployments.cancelText: Devices that haven't started won't run this job. Jobs that are already running finish first.
deployments.rebootText: The installer asked for a restart. The device restarts in the next maintenance window, or you can restart it yourself.

remote.title: Remote control
remote.subtitle: See and control the screen of a Windows computer or server from your browser, also on the sign-in screen and UAC prompts.
remote.connectHint: Opens the remote screen in a new tab.
remote.windowsOnly: Remote control is available for Windows devices. A terminal for Linux follows.
remote.connectText: Online Windows devices. The session opens in a new tab.
remote.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, user or IP address
remote.historyText: Every session with who started it, how long it lasted and how it ended. Kept for 400 days.

waiting.consent: Waiting for the user to allow the session

remote.waitingHint: This usually takes a few seconds.
remote.consentWait: The user sees a request on their screen. It is declined automatically in {{seconds}} seconds.

reasons.no_answer: The user did not answer in time.
reasons.consent_unavailable: The user is signed in, but the request could not be shown on their screen. Try again in a moment, or change the group to 'notify'.
reasons.user_ended: The user ended the session from the bar at the top of their screen.
reasons.viewer_timeout: The viewer did not open in time.
reasons.agent_timeout: The agent did not connect in time.
reasons.agent_closed: The connection to the agent was lost.
reasons.connection_lost: The connection to the server was lost.
reasons.unsupported: This device does not support remote control.
reasons.busy: The device already has the maximum number of sessions.
reasons.connect_failed: The agent could not reach the server for the session. Check that the reverse proxy passes WebSockets.
reasons.helper_failed: The screen of this computer could not be captured.
reasons.bad_message: A message failed its integrity check; the session was stopped.
reasons.bad_key: The session keys did not match.
reasons.internal: Something went wrong on the device.

remote.secureDesktopHint: The sign-in screen, the lock screen or a UAC prompt is shown.

consentHint.notify: The user sees a bar that you are connected and can end the session.
consentHint.ask: The user allowed this session and can end it from the bar on their screen.

remote.fromRemoteEmpty: Copy something on the remote computer and it appears here (and on your own clipboard, when the browser allows it).
remote.toRemoteHint: Ctrl+V in the viewer also pastes your own clipboard. 'Type it' enters the text as keystrokes, for fields that do not accept pasting (such as a sign-in screen).

notices.helper_restarting: The screen is reconnecting (the user may be signing in or out)…

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Compliance, missing patches and outdated software across your fleet. Export them as PDF or CSV, or have them mailed on a schedule.
reports.noCatalog: The winget catalog has not been downloaded yet, so outdated software cannot be checked. Refresh it on the Software page.

compliance.rule: A device is compliant when it was seen in the last {{offline}} days, has a patch scan, misses no security or critical updates older than {{grace}} days, has no outdated software and at least {{disk}}% free space on every disk.

software.note: Windows programs compared with the newest version in the winget catalog. Linux packages are in Missing patches.
software.none: All recognised software is up to date.
software.addHint: Adds the winget package to the software library and opens the deployment for these devices
software.ignore: Leave this program out of the reports
software.ignoredCount_one: {{count}} program is left out of the reports (see Settings).
software.ignoredCount_other: {{count}} programs are left out of the reports (see Settings).

schedules.title: Scheduled reports
schedules.subtitle: Reports mailed as PDF and/or CSV attachments, for example every Monday morning.
schedules.empty: No scheduled reports yet. Create one to get a weekly report in your mailbox.
schedules.name: Name
schedules.recipientsHint: E-mail addresses, separated by commas. At most 20.
schedules.sent_one: The report is queued for {{count}} recipient.
schedules.sent_other: The report is queued for {{count}} recipients.

settings.title: Compliance rules
settings.subtitle: When a device counts as compliant in the reports and on the dashboard.
settings.offlineHint: A device that was offline longer is not compliant.
settings.graceHint: Security and critical updates may be missing this long.
settings.diskHint: On every disk of 2 GB or more.
settings.ignoredHint: These winget packages do not count as outdated software, for example programs that update themselves or that you keep on an older version on purpose.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.subtitle: Devices that have been offline too long or are running out of disk space. Alerts close by themselves once the problem is gone.
alerts.none: No open alerts. Everything looks fine.

rules.title: Alert rules
rules.subtitle: When an alert opens, and who gets an e-mail about it.
rules.diskBelow: Less than {{percent}}% free space on a disk
rules.confirmDelete: Delete the alert rule "{{name}}" and its alerts?
rules.name: Name
rules.offlineHint: At least 5 minutes. Agents check in every minute.
rules.diskHint: Disks smaller than 2 GB are left out.
rules.recipientsHint: Up to 20 addresses, separated by commas. Leave empty to only show alerts here.
rules.notifyResolved: Also mail when an alert is resolved

proxy.title: Reverse proxy
proxy.subtitle: Run FleetWarden behind nginx, Caddy, HAProxy or Zoraxy: what the server sees, which proxies it trusts, ready-made configuration and an end-to-end test.
proxy.statusTitle: How this browser reaches the server
proxy.statusSubtitle: What the server sees for the request that loaded this page.
proxy.untrustedTitle: A proxy at {{peer}} forwards requests, but is not trusted
proxy.untrustedText: The server ignores its X-Forwarded-* headers. Audit logs and rate limits then see the proxy instead of the user, cookies are not marked secure and links point to http. Add this address to the trusted proxies and save.
proxy.localOnlyText: Only a proxy on this same machine can reach it. Is your proxy on another host (for example Zoraxy on a separate machine)? Let the server listen on the network by running this on the server, then add the proxy's address below. The setting is in {{file}}.
proxy.openText: Other machines can reach the server directly. Allow port access only from the proxy with a firewall, so that everyone goes through the proxy and its TLS.
proxy.publicUrlHint: The address users and agents use, such as https://fleet.example.com. Used for SSO, agent installers and links in e-mails. Empty: detected as {{url}}.
proxy.trustedHint: One IP address or network per line (CIDR). Only these may set X-Forwarded-For, -Proto and -Host. Always trusted from the server configuration: {{env}} (FW_TRUSTED_PROXIES in {{file}}).
proxy.hstsHint: Tells browsers to use only HTTPS for this domain for one year. Turn on once HTTPS works.
proxy.examplesSubtitle: Filled in with this server's address. Choose your proxy, copy the configuration and run the test below.
proxy.upstreamHint: Where the proxy reaches this server: host:port.
proxy.upstreamLocalOnly: The server only listens on {{listen}}, so a proxy on another host cannot reach this upstream. Change FW_LISTEN first (see above).
proxy.reqTitle: What the proxy must do for all features

web.title: Web interface and API
web.text: Forward everything under / to FleetWarden: the web interface, /api/ and /healthz.

agents.title: Agents
agents.text: /agent/ (enrollment, installers, downloads) must be reachable from the internet on port 443 for agents outside the office.

websocket.title: WebSockets
websocket.text: Agents (/agent/v1/ws), remote control and live updates use WebSockets: forward Upgrade and Connection headers.

headers.title: Forwarded headers
headers.text: Send X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host (or keep Host) and add the proxy to the trusted proxies.

tls.title: TLS
tls.text: The proxy terminates HTTPS with a valid certificate; agents refuse untrusted certificates. Redirect http:// to https://.

uploads.title: Large uploads
uploads.text: Software packages and agent installers up to {{gib}} GiB: raise the body size limit and stream uploads.

timeouts.title: Long connections
timeouts.text: Agents stay connected and remote sessions can take hours: idle timeouts of at least one hour (FleetWarden pings every 30 seconds).

zoraxy.s1: Ingress (called Status in older Zoraxy versions)
zoraxy.s1a: Inbound / Proxy Listening Port: 443, with "Use TLS to serve proxy request" on.
zoraxy.s1b: "Enable HTTP server on port 80" on, and "Force redirect HTTP request to HTTPS" on.
zoraxy.s1c: Port 80 and 443 forwarded to Zoraxy on your router.
zoraxy.target: Target IP Address or Domain Name with port
zoraxy.s2c: Leave "Proxy Target require TLS Connection" off: FleetWarden speaks plain HTTP behind the proxy.
zoraxy.s3: Advance Settings of the rule (also under HTTP Proxy > Edit)
zoraxy.s3a: Leave "Disable WebSocket" off: agents and remote control need WebSockets.
zoraxy.s3c: Turn "Refresh timeout on activity" on, so the timeout is an idle timeout and not a maximum duration of 5 minutes.
zoraxy.s3d: Leave "Block Common Exploits" off for this rule: it can block agent traffic and installer uploads.
zoraxy.s4a: Set an ACME e-mail, choose Let's Encrypt and request a certificate for {{domain}}.
zoraxy.s4ownA: Upload the certificate (full chain) and private key for {{domain}}.
zoraxy.s5a: Zoraxy sends X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Host and X-Real-Ip by itself; no custom headers needed. It has no upload limit.
zoraxy.s5b: Add Zoraxy's IP address to the trusted proxies above, save, and run the test.

proxy.testSubtitle: Checks the whole path end to end: from the server through the external URL (as an agent does) and from this browser.
proxy.testIntro: Save your settings first. The test reaches this server through the external base URL, checks the certificate, the forwarded headers, the agent endpoint and WebSockets, and then tests WebSockets and a 16 MB upload from this browser.
proxy.summaryPass: Everything works: web interface, agents, WebSockets and uploads go through the proxy correctly.
proxy.summaryFail: {{n}} check(s) failed. See the explanation per check.
proxy.skipped: Skipped because an earlier check failed or does not apply.

side.server: From the server through the external URL (agent path)

public_url.title: External base URL
public_url.warn: {{detail}} uses http://. Agents and sign-in then travel unencrypted; use https:// via the proxy.
public_url.fail: No external base URL set. Fill it in above and save, so agents and links use the address of the proxy.

dns.title: DNS
dns.fail: The domain does not resolve from the server. Create the DNS record, or add it to /etc/hosts for internal use.

tls.title: TLS certificate
tls.warn: Valid but expires soon (issuer, protocol, days left): {{detail}}. Check automatic renewal.
tls.fail: Not valid: {{detail}}. Agents refuse to connect. Use Let's Encrypt or a certificate from a trusted CA, issued for this domain.

reach.title: Server reachable through the proxy
reach.pass: The proxy forwards to this FleetWarden server.
reach.fail: Not reachable: {{detail}}. Check that the proxy runs, forwards to the upstream above, and that the server can reach its own external URL (with NAT you may need hairpin NAT or an internal DNS record).

peer_trusted.title: Proxy is trusted
peer_trusted.pass: The proxy connects from {{detail}} and is trusted.
peer_trusted.fail: The proxy connects from {{detail}}, which is not trusted. Add it to the trusted proxies and save.

forwarded_proto.title: X-Forwarded-Proto
forwarded_proto.pass: The proxy reports the scheme correctly ({{detail}}).
forwarded_proto.fail: Missing or wrong ({{detail}}). Let the proxy send X-Forwarded-Proto: https, otherwise cookies are not secure and links use http.

forwarded_host.title: Host / X-Forwarded-Host
forwarded_host.pass: The server sees the external host {{detail}}.
forwarded_host.warn: The server sees host {{detail}} instead of the external domain. Let the proxy keep the Host header or send X-Forwarded-Host.

forwarded_for.title: X-Forwarded-For
forwarded_for.fail: Not sent. The audit log and rate limits then see the proxy instead of the real user.

agent_hello.title: Agent endpoint
agent_hello.fail: /agent/v1/hello does not answer correctly: {{detail}}. Forward /agent/ to FleetWarden too.

websocket.title: WebSocket (agents, remote control)
websocket.pass: WebSocket upgrade and messages work through the proxy.
websocket.fail: The upgrade failed: {{detail}}. Forward the Upgrade and Connection headers (nginx: proxy_set_header Upgrade/Connection; Zoraxy: do not disable WebSocket).

http_redirect.title: http:// to https://
http_redirect.warn: http:// answers with status {{detail}} instead of a redirect to https://.

browser_https.title: This browser uses HTTPS
browser_https.warn: This page is loaded over {{detail}}. Open FleetWarden via https:// through the proxy.

browser_origin.title: Opened via the external URL
browser_origin.pass: This page is opened via the external base URL.
browser_origin.warn: This page is opened via {{detail}}, not the external base URL. The browser tests below then test that path.

browser_headers.title: Forwarded headers for this browser
browser_headers.warn: This browser connects directly ({{detail}}), not through a proxy.
browser_headers.fail: Not accepted as a trusted proxy request over HTTPS ({{detail}}). Check the trusted proxies and that the proxy sends X-Forwarded-Proto.

browser_websocket.title: WebSocket from this browser (remote control, live updates)
browser_websocket.fail: Failed ({{detail}}). Check WebSocket forwarding and the Host/Origin header in the proxy.

browser_upload.title: Upload of 16 MB (installers)
browser_upload.pass: Accepted ({{detail}}). Make sure the proxy limit is at least 2 GiB.
browser_upload.fail: Rejected ({{detail}}). Status 413 means the proxy body size limit is too low (nginx: client_max_body_size; Caddy: request_body max_size).

gateways.title: Secure gateway
gateways.subtitle: A small relay in the DMZ for agents outside your network. The management server stays internal: it opens the connection to the gateway itself.
gateways.editHint: Changing the address or URL reconnects the tunnel. Agents receive the new URL automatically.
gateways.paired: Gateway {{name}} is paired. The server connects to it now.
gateways.deleteText_one: {{count}} agent is connected through this gateway. It reconnects through another address when it can reach one. The gateway itself stays installed; reset its pairing to use it again.
gateways.deleteText_other: {{count}} agents are connected through this gateway. They reconnect through another address when they can reach one. The gateway itself stays installed; reset its pairing to use it again.
gateways.repairText: Needed after the gateway was reinstalled or reset. Run this on the gateway, then enter the new pairing code it shows:
gateways.repairHint: Use "Pair again" with a new code from the gateway.
gateways.name: Name
gateways.addressHint: How this server reaches the gateway in the DMZ: IP address or host name, port {{port}} unless you changed it.
gateways.publicUrlHint: The address agents on the internet use, for example https://agents.example.com.
gateways.pairingCodeHint: Shown at installation, or with "sudo fleetwarden-gateway pairing-code" on the gateway. It works once.
gateways.versionMismatch: The gateway runs {{gateway}}, the server {{server}}. Update the gateway with the same install command to keep them in step.

checks.tunnelOk: the server is connected to the gateway
checks.publicUrlOk: reaches this server through this gateway

checkCodes.error: not connected; see the error above
checkCodes.unreachable: not reachable from the management server. That can be normal when the server cannot reach its own public address (no hairpin NAT); test it from a device outside the network.
checkCodes.bad_answer: something answered, but not FleetWarden. Check the reverse proxy in front of the gateway.
checkCodes.not_via_gateway: reaches this server, but not through this gateway. Point the URL at the gateway.

linkErrors.gateway_key_changed: The gateway has a new key
linkErrors.paired_with_other_server: The gateway is paired with another server
linkErrors.gateway_proof_invalid: The gateway could not prove its identity

flow.explain: Agents trust only the server key they pinned at enrollment, so the gateway passes their signed messages on without being able to change them. Remote control stays end-to-end encrypted.

setup.title: Set up a gateway
setup.subtitle: Three steps on a Debian 13 machine in your DMZ.
setup.show: Show the steps to add another gateway
setup.installHint: Run this on the DMZ machine. The installer asks how agents reach it: behind your reverse proxy, with your own certificate, or with a Let's Encrypt certificate it requests itself.
setup.firewallIn: Internet to gateway: TCP 443 (or the port of your reverse proxy).
setup.firewallTunnel: Management server to gateway: TCP {{port}} (the tunnel). Allow only the server's address.
setup.firewallNone: No rule from the DMZ into your network is needed.
setup.pairHint: The installer shows a one-time pairing code. You can show it again with:

endpoints.title: Addresses agents use
endpoints.subtitle: Sent to every agent. An agent tries them in this order and moves on when one does not answer, so laptops switch between office and home by themselves.
endpoints.none: No gateway yet: agents only use the address they were installed with.
endpoints.noServerUrl: Set the external base URL of this server (Settings or Reverse proxy) so agents also get the internal address. Without it they keep the address they were installed with.

gateways.versionMismatchUpdate: The gateway runs {{gateway}}, the server {{server}}. Update the gateway so they stay in step.
gateways.updateRequested: Gateway {{name}} installs {{version}} now. The tunnel drops for a moment while it restarts.

configs.title: Configurations
configs.subtitle: Settings that agents apply to the devices of a group and keep in place: they check every {{minutes}} minutes and put back what was changed.
configs.emptyText: Set a start page in every browser, change registry settings or run a script on a group of devices. It also works on computers that are not in a domain.

typeHints.browser: Start page, home button, password manager and forced extensions for Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
typeHints.registry: Registry values for the computer (HKLM) or for every user who logs on (HKCU).
typeHints.script: A PowerShell, cmd, bash or sh script that runs once, at startup, at logon or on an interval.
typeHints.drives: Map network drives such as H: for every user who logs on, also on PCs without a domain.
typeHints.printers: Shared printers from a print server and TCP/IP printers, with their driver and the default printer.
typeHints.desktop: Wallpaper for every user and locking the PC after a time without input.
typeHints.power: When the screen turns off and the PC sleeps or hibernates, on mains power and on battery.
typeHints.admins: Accounts and groups that are added to the local Administrators group.
typeHints.firewall: Windows Firewall rules that allow or block traffic by port, address or program.

configs.noGroupsHint: Pick at least one group, otherwise no device gets this configuration.
configs.repairedTitle_one: Settings were changed outside FleetWarden on {{count}} device
configs.repairedTitle_other: Settings were changed outside FleetWarden on {{count}} devices
configs.repairedHint: The agent put them back. If this keeps happening, a user or another tool keeps changing them.
configs.repairedDomain: On domain computers this usually means a Group Policy (GPO) sets the same thing. Remove it from the GPO or from this configuration, otherwise both keep overwriting each other.
configs.noDevicesHint: No devices of this platform in the assigned groups.
configs.runsHint: The job log of the last 90 days. Click a run to see its output.
configs.noRuns: The script has not run yet.
configs.deleteText: Delete “{{name}}”? Agents remove the browser policies and registry values it set the next time they check in. Scripts that already ran are not undone.
configs.name: Name
configs.priorityHint: Lower numbers apply first. When two configurations set the same thing, the higher number wins.
configs.enabledHint: When off, agents remove the settings of this configuration.
configs.assignHint: Devices of these groups get the configuration, also devices that join later.
configs.noSettingsAccess: You may not see the settings of this configuration.
configs.deviceHint: The configurations of this device's group, in the order they apply.
configs.deviceEmpty: No configurations apply to this device.

browser.homepageHint: The page of the home button.
browser.startupRestore: Continue where the user left off
browser.passwordManagerHint: Off stops the browser from offering to save passwords.
browser.extensionsHint: Installed automatically; users cannot remove them.
browser.chromiumExtensionsHint: The 32-letter ID from the web store address, one per line.
browser.firefoxExtensionsHint: The https link to the .xpi file, one per line.
browser.advancedHint: Any other policy by its documented name, as a JSON object per browser. See the policy lists of Chrome, Edge and Firefox.
browser.invalidJson: Not a valid JSON object; the last valid text is kept.

registry.name: Value name
registry.hint: HKLM applies to the computer. HKCU applies to every user who logs on: the agent sets it while they are logged on and again at every logon.
registry.keep: Keep values when the configuration is removed
registry.keepHint: Normally the agent removes the values it set when the configuration no longer applies.

script.runAsSystemHint: Full rights on the computer, no access to network shares of the user.
script.runAsUserHint: Runs in the session of every logged-on user, with their rights, without a window.

triggerHints.once: Runs once per device (or user). A changed script runs again; a failed run is tried up to three times.
triggerHints.startup: Runs after every start of the device.
triggerHints.logon: Runs when a user logs on.

script.contentHint: Exit code 0 means success. The last 8,000 characters of the output are kept in the job log.

drives.label: Name in Explorer
drives.hint: The agent maps the drives in the session of every user who logs on and puts them back when they are removed. %USERNAME% and %USERDOMAIN% are filled in per user. Windows connects with the user's own sign-in: on a PC without a domain, Windows asks for the password once when the drive is opened, unless the user has the same account on the server.

printers.name: Printer name
printers.namePlaceholder: Name on the PC, e.g. Floor 2
printers.driverHint: The exact name of the driver, as Windows shows it. Built in: Microsoft IPP Class Driver, Generic / Text Only.
printers.sharedDriverHint: Install this driver first, so users who are no administrator can connect (Windows blocks drivers from print servers for them).
printers.driverInfHint: For a driver that is not in Windows yet. A path on the PC or on a share the computer can read.
printers.default: Make this the default printer of every user
printers.hint: The agent adds the printers and their drivers, and adds them again when they are removed. Printers it added are removed when the configuration no longer applies.

scopeHints.device: Windows adds it to the printers of every user the next time they log on.
scopeHints.user: Added right away in the session of each logged-on user.

configs.noProfilesHint: Put the configuration in at least one profile, otherwise no device gets it.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.subtitle: A profile bundles configurations. Assign it to device groups: every device in those groups gets all its configurations, also PCs without a domain.
profiles.pickHint: Devices in the groups of these profiles get the configuration.
profiles.none: There are no profiles yet. Make one under Profiles, or save now and add it to a profile later.
profiles.emptyText: Bundle configurations such as a start page, network drives and printers in a profile, and assign it to device groups.
profiles.itemsHint: The configurations in this profile. A configuration can be in several profiles.
profiles.enabledHint: Turned off, devices no longer get the configurations through this profile.
profiles.assignHint: Devices in these groups get every configuration of the profile, also devices that join later.
profiles.noGroupsHint: Pick at least one group, otherwise no device gets this profile.
profiles.deleteText: {{name}} is deleted. Its configurations stay, but devices that got them only through this profile remove their settings.

desktop.wallpaperHint: An image on the PC or on a share every user can read. Empty: not managed.
desktop.lockHint: Locks the PC after this many minutes without input. 0: not managed.
desktop.hint: These are Windows policies: users cannot change them. A new wallpaper shows at the next sign-in.

power.hint: Empty is not managed, 0 is never. The settings apply at once and users cannot change them; when they are no longer configured, users can change them again.

admins.membersHint: One per line: DOMAIN\name, a local account, AzureAD\user@domain or a SID.
admins.hint: Members that FleetWarden added are removed again when they are no longer configured. Other members of the group stay.

firewall.name: Name
firewall.hint: The rules are in the Windows Firewall group "FleetWarden". Someone who changes or removes one gets it back; rules that are no longer configured are removed.

drivers.title: Drivers & firmware
drivers.subtitle: Your own repository of driver and firmware updates. Devices report what they can get; nothing is downloaded until you add it here.

listHints.available: Offered to at least one of your devices by Windows Update, fwupd or a vendor BIOS catalog. Add an update to the repository to let the server download it.
listHints.repository: Stored on this server. Devices install these in the patch window of their policy, or right away from a device's Drivers tab.
listHints.rejected: Hidden from the available list. Restore one to see it again.

empty.available: No new driver or firmware updates. Devices report them with each update scan.

stats.devices: {{devices}} device(s) with an update on offer · {{scanned}} scanned

drivers.failedHint: {{count}} download(s) failed. Open the update to see why, and try again.
drivers.search: Search by name, vendor, class or hardware ID
drivers.noDevices: No device in your scope reports this update.
drivers.firmwareWarning: Firmware is only installed on devices whose patch policy allows firmware. Keep the device on power during the restart; on Windows BitLocker is suspended for that restart.
drivers.notDownloadedHint: Not downloaded yet. Adding it to the repository downloads it once from the vendor to this server; devices then get it from here.
drivers.offeredHint: Only updates in the repository can be installed. Others need an administrator to add them under Drivers & firmware first.
drivers.installStarted: Install started. Follow it on the Updates tab.
drivers.upToDate: No driver or firmware updates on offer.
drivers.deviceNoPolicy: The device's group has no patch policy, so nothing is installed automatically. You can still install repository updates by hand.

vendors.title: BIOS from the vendor catalogs
vendors.hint: Once a day the server reads the BIOS catalogs of Dell, HP and Lenovo for the models among your Windows devices. Only the catalogs are read: a BIOS update is offered under Available and only downloaded after you add it to the repository.

about.dell: Matched on the system ID (SKU) and the BIOS version. Installed with the Dell Update Package, silently.
about.hp: Matched on the platform ID (baseboard) and the ROM family. Installed with HP's flash tool from the SoftPaq, silently.
about.lenovo: Matched on the machine type and the BIOS level. Installed with Lenovo's BIOS update utility, silently.

vendors.notYet: Not yet since the server started
vendors.daily: Catalogs are read again after 24 hours, and right away for a new model.
vendors.unmatched: Some devices do not report their system ID or baseboard yet ({{list}}). They are matched once their agent is updated and has sent a new inventory.
vendors.catalogsHint: The vendor catalogs read for the models of your devices.
vendors.none: No Dell, HP or Lenovo Windows devices with a known model yet.

uploads.title: Own driver packages
uploads.hint: Packages you upload yourself: a driver as a .zip or .cab with its .inf, a vendor program (.exe) with silent arguments, or a firmware cabinet for fwupd. They are stored right away and offered to the devices the target matches.
uploads.confirmDelete: Delete "{{title}}"? Devices no longer get it.
uploads.drop: Drop a .zip, .cab or .exe here (at most 2 GB)
uploads.name: Name
uploads.platformHint: A .zip or .exe is for Windows; a .cab is a Windows driver or a fwupd firmware cabinet.
uploads.manufacturerHint: Empty for every manufacturer. Compared with the device's inventory, ignoring case.
uploads.modelHint: Empty for every model, e.g. "Latitude 7450" or "20XW".
uploads.argumentsHint: Passed to the program, e.g. /s for a Dell Update Package. Exit codes 0, 3010 and 1641 mean success.

how.inf: The agent unpacks the package and installs every .inf in it with pnputil.
how.exe: The agent runs the program as SYSTEM with the arguments above.
how.fwupd: The agent installs the cabinet with fwupdmgr on the devices it fits.

manage.title: Manage
manage.noTakeover: The user keeps working: nothing here takes over the screen.
manage.offline: Processes, services, logs and files are available while the agent is connected.

processes.hint: Running programs with their CPU and memory use, measured over half a second.
processes.search: Search by name, PID, user or command line
processes.name: Name
processes.stopBody: End {{name}} (PID {{pid}})? Unsaved work in this program is lost.
processes.protected: Protected: Windows, the system or the agent itself needs this process.
processes.more: {{count}} more; narrow the search to see them.

services.hintWindows: Windows services. Start, stop and restart them, or change how they start.
services.hintLinux: systemd services. Start, stop and restart them, or change whether they start at boot.
services.protected: This is the agent's own service; it is not changed from here.
services.confirmBody: Programs and users that depend on this service may stop working while it is not running.

logs.hintWindows: Windows event logs, newest first. Click an event for the full text.
logs.hintLinux: The systemd journal, newest first. Click an entry for the full text.
logs.truncated: The newest {{count}} events; there are more. Narrow the filter.

files.hint: Browse the file system as SYSTEM (Windows) or root (Linux). Download files or whole folders, upload files.
files.name: Name
files.truncated: Only the first 10,000 entries are shown.
files.dropHint: Tip: drop files on the list to upload them to this folder.
files.deleteFolderBody: Delete the folder {{path}} and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
files.overwriteBody: Some of these files already exist in this folder. Replace them?
files.transfersHint: Downloads stay available for an hour.
